page: Microsoft Azure L48as_v3 is an x86_64 architecture server powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled, running at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz. The system is equipped with 384.0 GB of RAM, providing a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8 GB per core. Storage is a key highlight, featuring 12,012 GB of local NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark data indicates strong multi-core processing capabilities, with stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core scores placing in the top 25%. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, ray tracing, and image processing also demonstrate strong performance. Memory performance is robust, with Passmark memory scores in the top tier, while memory bandwidth tests for both cached and uncached reads and writes fall within the average range. Cryptographic operations perform strongly, supported by hardware-accelerated AES and SHA instruction sets.

Given the massive 12 TB of local NVMe SSD storage bundled with 384 GB of RAM, this server offers high resource density for data-intensive operations without requiring external storage attachments. The lack of a dedicated GPU limits its utility for heavy deep learning training, but it is highly optimized for large-scale databases, data warehousing, high-throughput transactional systems, and memory-intensive analytics workloads.
description: The Microsoft Azure L48as_v3 is an x86_64 server from the LASv3 family, powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 7763 processor. It delivers 48 vCPUs across 24 physical cores at 3.525 GHz, paired with 384 GB of RAM and an extensive 12,012 GB local NVMe SSD. This hardware configuration yields strong multi-core CPU and memory benchmark results, placing in the top 25% for multi-threaded processing, cryptography, and image manipulation. While memory bandwidth and single-core performance remain in the average tier, the massive local storage capacity and high memory-to-core ratio make this instance highly cost-efficient for storage-heavy and memory-intensive workloads. It is best suited for large-scale relational databases, NoSQL platforms, data warehousing, and high-throughput transactional applications.
